book-10-math_ch_3_topic_rational_inequal.detailed_overview:
The real number system provides a complete continuum without gaps (Dedekind completeness). Radicals represent fractional exponents, and simplifying surds through rationalization establishes standardized numerical values.

Key Takeaway: Rational numbers have repeating or terminating decimals; radicals in denominators must be rationalized using algebraic conjugates.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Precise land parcel boundary surveys in Ethiopia's cadastre system use rational coordinates and radical distance triangulation.

topics_covered.title: 3.3 Rational Inequalities
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.3 Rational Inequalities
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Fractional inequalities P(x)/Q(x) ≥ 0, critical points from numerator and denominator, domain restrictions.
• Number System Hierarchy: ℕ (Natural) ⊂ 𝕎 (Whole) ⊂ ℤ (Integers) ⊂ ℚ (Rationals) ⊂ ℝ (Real Numbers). Complex numbers ℂ contain all real and imaginary roots.

• Rational vs. Irrational Numbers: Rational numbers can be written as a/b (b ≠ 0) with terminating or repeating decimals. Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as a fraction and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals (e.g. √2, π, e).
• Proof of Irrationality of √2: By contradiction: assume √2 = a/b in lowest terms. 2b² = a² ⇒ a is even ⇒ 4k² = 2b² ⇒ b is even. Contradicts assumption of lowest terms.
• Radical Algebraic Rules: √(ab) = √a·√b and √(a/b) = √a/√b for a, b ≥ 0. Rationalizing denominators: multiply by conjugate (√a - √b) / (√a - √b) to eliminate surds from denominator.
• Absolute Value Properties: |x| = x if x ≥ 0, and -x if x < 0. Triangle inequality: |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|. Distance between points a and b is |a - b|.
key_points: Between any two distinct rational numbers, there are infinitely many rational and irrational numbers (dense property of ℝ).
√x² = |x|, NOT simply x. If x is negative, √((-3)²) = |-3| = 3.
Never cancel across addition inside a radical: √(a² + b²) ≠ a + b.

book-10-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.topic_title: Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
book-10-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables (Unit 3: Unit 3: Solving Inequalities). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 3.4 Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.4 Systems of Linear Inequalities in Two Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Boundary lines, half-planes, shaded feasible regions, and corner-point method.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

key_concepts.explanation: The solutions to f(x) = 0 correspond directly to the x-intercepts of the curve y = f(x). Intersections of two curves f(x) = g(x) represent their simultaneous solution set.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Two roads crossing on a map: the intersection point satisfies the coordinates of both roads simultaneously.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?

topics_covered.title: 4.3 Slope of a Line and Angle of Inclination
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.3 Slope of a Line and Angle of Inclination
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: m = tan θ = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1), positive/negative/zero/undefined slopes, and collinearity tests.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-10-math_ch_4_topic_distance_formula.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Distance Formula and Midpoint in Cartesian Plane (Unit 4: Unit 4: Coordinate Geometry). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_4_topic_distance_formula.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Distance Formula and Midpoint in Cartesian Plane
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Distance Formula and Midpoint in Cartesian Plane
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: d = √[(x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²], midpoint coordinates M, and perimeter/area of polygons.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: 3D Space Coordinates
core_formulas_rules.explanation: 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications and SI units apply.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications and SI units apply.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Scalar (Dot) Product
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications and SI units apply.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Vector (Cross) Product
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications and SI units apply.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Equations of Lines & Planes
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Standard Ethiopian curriculum specifications and SI units apply.

topics_covered.topic_title: 5.2 Properties of Chords, Tangents and Secants
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Perpendicular from center bisects chord, equal chords are equidistant, tangent is perpendicular to radius.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 5.3 Angle Theorems in Circles
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.3 Angle Theorems in Circles
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Angle subtended at center is double angle at circumference, angles in same segment are equal, angle in semicircle is 90°.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-10-math_ch_5_topic_triangles__congr.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 5.1 Triangles: Congruence and Similarity Theorems
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 Triangles: Congruence and Similarity Theorems
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: SAS, SSS, ASA, AAS congruence criteria; AA, SAS, SSS similarity theorems, Thales theorem.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

book-10-math_ch_5_topic_properties_of_ch.topic_title: Properties of Chords, Tangents and Secants
book-10-math_ch_5_topic_properties_of_ch.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Properties of Chords, Tangents and Secants (Unit 5: Unit 5: Plane Geometry). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_5_topic_properties_of_ch.detailed_overview:
Limits describe the local behavior of a function near a point rather than at the point itself. This foundation allows calculus to rigorously evaluate instantaneous rates and areas without dividing by zero.

Key Takeaway: Continuity requires f(c) to be defined, the two-sided limit to exist, and both values to match exactly.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Continuous mathematical models are utilized in hydrology to track water discharge rates through the GERD dam spillways during seasonal flood peaks.

topics_covered.title: 5.2 Properties of Chords, Tangents and Secants
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.2 Properties of Chords, Tangents and Secants
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Perpendicular from center bisects chord, equal chords are equidistant, tangent is perpendicular to radius.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

book-10-math_ch_5_topic_cyclic_quadrilat.topic_title: Cyclic Quadrilaterals and Power of a Point Theorem
book-10-math_ch_5_topic_cyclic_quadrilat.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Cyclic Quadrilaterals and Power of a Point Theorem (Unit 5: Unit 5: Plane Geometry). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_5_topic_cyclic_quadrilat.detailed_overview:
Limits describe the local behavior of a function near a point rather than at the point itself. This foundation allows calculus to rigorously evaluate instantaneous rates and areas without dividing by zero.

Key Takeaway: Continuity requires f(c) to be defined, the two-sided limit to exist, and both values to match exactly.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Continuous mathematical models are utilized in hydrology to track water discharge rates through the GERD dam spillways during seasonal flood peaks.

topics_covered.title: 5.4 Cyclic Quadrilaterals and Power of a Point Theorem
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.4 Cyclic Quadrilaterals and Power of a Point Theorem
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°, intersecting chords theorem, tangent-secant theorem.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Radian Measure and Degree Conversion
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Radian Measure and Degree Conversion
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Definition of radian, π rad = 180°, arc length s = rθ, and area of circular sector A = 0.5r²θ.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Function Mapping Machine: Input x ──> [Function f(x)] ──> Output y ──> [Inverse Function f⁻¹(y)] ──> Returns original x.

topics_covered.key_takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Coordinates on unit circle (cos θ, sin θ), ASTC sign rule in 4 quadrants, and reference angles.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: 3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: 3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: Right-Hand Rule for Cross Product: Index finger = u, Middle finger = v, Thumb points perpendicular = u × v. Normal to plane containing u and v.
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Right-Hand Rule for Cross Product: Index finger = u, Middle finger = v, Thumb points perpendicular = u × v. Normal to plane containing u and v.
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Radian Measure and Degree Conversion
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Definition of radian, π rad = 180°, arc length s = rθ, and area of circular sector A = 0.5r²θ.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.

book-10-math_ch_6_topic_6_2_trigonometri.unit_summary: Curriculum Study Notes: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle. • Curriculum Focus: Coordinates on unit circle (cos θ, sin θ), ASTC sign rule in 4 quadrants, and reference angles.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Coordinates on unit circle (cos θ, sin θ), ASTC sign rule in 4 quadrants, and reference angles.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Periodic behavior, amplitude, period (2π for sin/cos, π for tan), phase shift, and vertical translation.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

topics_covered.title: 6.5 Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.5 Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Solving oblique triangles using a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C and c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C, bearings and distances.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.

book-10-math_ch_6_topic_trigonometric_ra.topic_title: Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_trigonometric_ra.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle (Unit 6: Unit 6: Trigonometric Functions). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_trigonometric_ra.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and the Unit Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Coordinates on unit circle (cos θ, sin θ), ASTC sign rule in 4 quadrants, and reference angles.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).

• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.

book-10-math_ch_6_topic_graphs_of_sine__.topic_title: Graphs of Sine, Cosine and Tangent Functions
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_graphs_of_sine__.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Graphs of Sine, Cosine and Tangent Functions (Unit 6: Unit 6: Trigonometric Functions). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_graphs_of_sine__.detailed_overview:
Limits describe the local behavior of a function near a point rather than at the point itself. This foundation allows calculus to rigorously evaluate instantaneous rates and areas without dividing by zero.

Key Takeaway: Continuity requires f(c) to be defined, the two-sided limit to exist, and both values to match exactly.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Continuous mathematical models are utilized in hydrology to track water discharge rates through the GERD dam spillways during seasonal flood peaks.

topics_covered.title: 6.4 Graphs of Sine, Cosine and Tangent Functions
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.4 Graphs of Sine, Cosine and Tangent Functions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Periodic behavior, amplitude, period (2π for sin/cos, π for tan), phase shift, and vertical translation.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

book-10-math_ch_6_topic_applications__la.topic_title: Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_applications__la.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines (Unit 6: Unit 6: Trigonometric Functions). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_6_topic_applications__la.detailed_overview:
Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

Key Takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.

topics_covered.title: 6.5 Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.5 Applications: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Solving oblique triangles using a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C and c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C, bearings and distances.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

topics_covered.title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² for center (h, k) and radius r; circle centered at origin x² + y² = r².
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-10-math_ch_7_topic_7_1_standard_equ.unit_summary: Curriculum Study Notes: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle. • Curriculum Focus: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² for center (h, k) and radius r; circle centered at origin x² + y² = r².
book-10-math_ch_7_topic_7_1_standard_equ.detailed_overview: Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

topics_covered.title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² for center (h, k) and radius r; circle centered at origin x² + y² = r².
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

book-10-math_ch_7_topic_7_3_tangent_line.detailed_overview: Limits describe the local behavior of a function near a point rather than at the point itself. This foundation allows calculus to rigorously evaluate instantaneous rates and areas without dividing by zero.

topics_covered.title: 7.3 Tangent Lines to a Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.3 Tangent Lines to a Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Equation of tangent line at given point (x1, y1) on circle, length of tangents from external point.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?

short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Secant (2 intersection points), tangent (1 point, Δ = 0), and non-intersecting line (Δ < 0).
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.

book-10-math_ch_7_topic_standard_equatio.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Standard Equation of a Circle (Unit 7: Unit 7: Circles). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 10 Mathematics syllabus.
book-10-math_ch_7_topic_standard_equatio.detailed_overview:
Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

Key Takeaway: The Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the unit circle define all trigonometric transformations.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Trigonometric triangulation is used by the Ethiopian Geospatial Information Institute for topological elevation mapping of the Semien and Bale mountain ranges.

topics_covered.title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.1 Standard Equation of a Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² for center (h, k) and radius r; circle centered at origin x² + y² = r².
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

book-10-math_ch_7_topic_tangent_lines_to.detailed_overview:
Limits describe the local behavior of a function near a point rather than at the point itself. This foundation allows calculus to rigorously evaluate instantaneous rates and areas without dividing by zero.

Key Takeaway: Continuity requires f(c) to be defined, the two-sided limit to exist, and both values to match exactly.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Continuous mathematical models are utilized in hydrology to track water discharge rates through the GERD dam spillways during seasonal flood peaks.

topics_covered.title: 7.3 Tangent Lines to a Circle
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.3 Tangent Lines to a Circle
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Equation of tangent line at given point (x1, y1) on circle, length of tangents from external point.
• Definition of Limit: lim_{x→c} f(x) = L means f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from both sides. One-sided limits must agree: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = L.
• Limit Laws: Limits distribute linearly across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-zero division: lim[f(x)/g(x)] = [lim f(x)] / [lim g(x)] provided lim g(x) ≠ 0.

• Resolving 0/0 Indeterminate Forms: 1) Factoring and canceling common factors; 2) Conjugate rationalization for radicals: multiply numerator/denominator by conjugate (√A + B); 3) Standard trig limits: lim_{x→0} [sin x / x] = 1.

• Limits at Infinity (Asymptotes): For rational functions P(x)/Q(x): if deg(P) < deg(Q), lim = 0 (horizontal asymptote y = 0); if deg(P) = deg(Q), lim = ratio of leading coefficients; if deg(P) > deg(Q), limit is ±∞.
• Continuity Criteria: A function f is continuous at x = c if and only if: 1) f(c) is defined; 2) lim_{x→c} f(x) exists; 3) lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).
key_points: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs when both numerator and denominator share a common factor (x - c).
Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator equals zero after all common factors are simplified.
Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT): If f is continuous on [a, b] and k is between f(a) and f(b), there exists at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f(c) = k.

key_concepts.explanation: A function is defined only on the set of real numbers where denominators are non-zero, radicands of even roots are non-negative, and logarithmic arguments are strictly positive.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Think of domain like an electrical device's voltage specification: plug in a prohibited number and the function "shorts out" (undefined).

key_concepts.explanation: Operations such as squaring both sides or multiplying by expressions containing variables can introduce extraneous solutions or eliminate valid roots.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Squaring (-3) and (3) both equal 9; going backwards introduces a "ghost" solution that must be screened.

key_concepts.explanation: The solutions to f(x) = 0 correspond directly to the x-intercepts of the curve y = f(x). Intersections of two curves f(x) = g(x) represent their simultaneous solution set.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Two roads crossing on a map: the intersection point satisfies the coordinates of both roads simultaneously.

euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Always plug every candidate answer back into the ORIGINAL equation! If x = -2 results in √(-2) or a negative value equal to a square root, it must be discarded.

euee_exam_tips.trap: Multiplying an Inequality by a Negative Variable
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Never multiply both sides of an inequality by an unknown variable x unless you partition the problem into positive and negative cases. Use sign charts (critical value method) instead!
Before solving lengthy quadratics, check if any option matches sum = -b/a and product = c/a. This often answers the question in under 15 seconds.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.
