topics_covered.topic_title: 3.2 Matrix Operations: Addition, Scalar & Multiplication
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Commutative/associative properties of addition, scalar distribution, row-column dot product multiplication criteria.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_3_6_inverse_of_a.unit_summary: Curriculum Study Notes: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations. • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_3_6_inverse_of_a.detailed_overview: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_concepts_of_a_ma.topic_title: Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_concepts_of_a_ma.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations (Unit 3: Unit 3: Matrices). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_concepts_of_a_ma.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables (Unit 3: Unit 3: Matrices). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.detailed_overview:
Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).

Key Takeaway: The n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is linear (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d), and its sum is S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Graduated tax brackets and tiered agricultural tariffs in Ethiopia use arithmetic stepped progressions.

topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_inverse_of_a_squ.topic_title: Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_inverse_of_a_squ.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations (Unit 3: Unit 3: Matrices). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_inverse_of_a_squ.detailed_overview:
Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

Key Takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_applications_of_.detailed_overview:
Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

Key Takeaway: The Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the unit circle define all trigonometric transformations.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.
topics_covered.explanation: Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: Gauss Pairing Method: (a_1 + a_n) = (a_2 + a_{n-1}) = (a_3 + a_{n-2}). With n terms, there are n/2 such pairs, yielding S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Gauss Pairing Method: (a_1 + a_n) = (a_2 + a_{n-1}) = (a_3 + a_{n-2}). With n terms, there are n/2 such pairs, yielding S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Graduated tax brackets and tiered agricultural tariffs in Ethiopia use arithmetic stepped progressions.
topics_covered.exam_focus: EUEE questions frequently give two non-consecutive terms (e.g. a_4 = 15, a_10 = 39) and ask for d, a_1, or S_20.
topics_covered.key_takeaway: The n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is linear (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d), and its sum is S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cofactor matrix, classical adjoint adj(A) = C^T, and inversion formula A^-1 = (1/det(A)) adj(A).
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

topics_covered.title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Area of triangles via coordinates, collinearity test of three points, and equation of lines through two points.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: 3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: 3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cofactor matrix, classical adjoint adj(A) = C^T, and inversion formula A^-1 = (1/det(A)) adj(A).
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

topics_covered.title: 4.5 Cramer Rule for Linear Systems
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.5 Cramer Rule for Linear Systems
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Determinant quotient formula xi = det(Ai)/det(A) for non-singular square systems and solvability checks.
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-11-math_ch_4_topic_determinants_of_.detailed_overview:
Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).

Key Takeaway: The n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is linear (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d), and its sum is S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Graduated tax brackets and tiered agricultural tariffs in Ethiopia use arithmetic stepped progressions.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.

book-11-math_ch_4_topic_adjoint_matrix_a.detailed_overview:
Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

Key Takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cofactor matrix, classical adjoint adj(A) = C^T, and inversion formula A^-1 = (1/det(A)) adj(A).
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

book-11-math_ch_4_topic_cramer_rule_for_.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Cramer Rule for Linear Systems (Unit 4: Unit 4: Determinants and Their Properties). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_4_topic_cramer_rule_for_.detailed_overview:
Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

Key Takeaway: The Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the unit circle define all trigonometric transformations.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Trigonometric triangulation is used by the Ethiopian Geospatial Information Institute for topological elevation mapping of the Semien and Bale mountain ranges.

topics_covered.title: 4.5 Cramer Rule for Linear Systems
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.5 Cramer Rule for Linear Systems
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Determinant quotient formula xi = det(Ai)/det(A) for non-singular square systems and solvability checks.
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

book-11-math_ch_4_topic_applications_of_.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Applications of Determinants in Geometry (Unit 4: Unit 4: Determinants and Their Properties). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_4_topic_applications_of_.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
topics_covered.topic_title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Area of triangles via coordinates, collinearity test of three points, and equation of lines through two points.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

topics_covered.title: 5.1 Revision on Vectors and Scalars
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 Revision on Vectors and Scalars
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Directed line segments, magnitude ||v||, direction angle, position vectors, and zero vector.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).

• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

key_concepts.explanation: A function is defined only on the set of real numbers where denominators are non-zero, radicands of even roots are non-negative, and logarithmic arguments are strictly positive.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Think of domain like an electrical device's voltage specification: plug in a prohibited number and the function "shorts out" (undefined).

key_concepts.explanation: Operations such as squaring both sides or multiplying by expressions containing variables can introduce extraneous solutions or eliminate valid roots.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Squaring (-3) and (3) both equal 9; going backwards introduces a "ghost" solution that must be screened.

key_concepts.explanation: The solutions to f(x) = 0 correspond directly to the x-intercepts of the curve y = f(x). Intersections of two curves f(x) = g(x) represent their simultaneous solution set.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Two roads crossing on a map: the intersection point satisfies the coordinates of both roads simultaneously.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Quadratic Formula & Nature of Roots: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a)
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates root characteristics: Δ > 0 (two distinct real roots), Δ = 0 (repeated real root), Δ < 0 (complex conjugate roots).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Valid for any quadratic equation in canonical form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Vieta's Formulas: Sum of roots = -b/a, Product of roots = c/a
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Enables rapid verification of roots and construction of quadratic polynomials without lengthy factoring.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Applicable to any degree-2 polynomial with real or complex coefficients.

core_formulas_rules.explanation: Calculates Euclidean distance and midpoint coordinates in the 2D Cartesian coordinate plane.
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Applies to any points A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂).

euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Always plug every candidate answer back into the ORIGINAL equation! If x = -2 results in √(-2) or a negative value equal to a square root, it must be discarded.

euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Never multiply both sides of an inequality by an unknown variable x unless you partition the problem into positive and negative cases. Use sign charts (critical value method) instead!
Before solving lengthy quadratics, check if any option matches sum = -b/a and product = c/a. This often answers the question in under 15 seconds.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

topics_covered.title: 5.2 Algebraic Representation and Operations in R2 and R3
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.2 Algebraic Representation and Operations in R2 and R3
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Component form (x, y, z), unit base vectors i, j, k, scalar multiplication, and vector linear combinations.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

book-11-math_ch_5_topic_applications_of_.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

topics_covered.title: 5.5 Applications of Dot and Cross Products
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.5 Applications of Dot and Cross Products
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Work done, torque, area of parallelogram, area of triangle, and volume of parallelepiped via scalar triple product.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Preservation of distance, angle measures, and collinearity in plane geometric transformations.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.
topics_covered.explanation: Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: Gauss Pairing Method: (a_1 + a_n) = (a_2 + a_{n-1}) = (a_3 + a_{n-2}). With n terms, there are n/2 such pairs, yielding S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Gauss Pairing Method: (a_1 + a_n) = (a_2 + a_{n-1}) = (a_3 + a_{n-2}). With n terms, there are n/2 such pairs, yielding S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Graduated tax brackets and tiered agricultural tariffs in Ethiopia use arithmetic stepped progressions.
topics_covered.exam_focus: EUEE questions frequently give two non-consecutive terms (e.g. a_4 = 15, a_10 = 39) and ask for d, a_1, or S_20.
topics_covered.key_takeaway: The n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is linear (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d), and its sum is S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).

key_concepts.explanation: A function is defined only on the set of real numbers where denominators are non-zero, radicands of even roots are non-negative, and logarithmic arguments are strictly positive.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Think of domain like an electrical device's voltage specification: plug in a prohibited number and the function "shorts out" (undefined).

key_concepts.explanation: Operations such as squaring both sides or multiplying by expressions containing variables can introduce extraneous solutions or eliminate valid roots.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Squaring (-3) and (3) both equal 9; going backwards introduces a "ghost" solution that must be screened.

key_concepts.explanation: The solutions to f(x) = 0 correspond directly to the x-intercepts of the curve y = f(x). Intersections of two curves f(x) = g(x) represent their simultaneous solution set.
key_concepts.illustration_analogy: Two roads crossing on a map: the intersection point satisfies the coordinates of both roads simultaneously.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Quadratic Formula & Nature of Roots: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a)
core_formulas_rules.explanation: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates root characteristics: Δ > 0 (two distinct real roots), Δ = 0 (repeated real root), Δ < 0 (complex conjugate roots).
core_formulas_rules.units_conditions: Valid for any quadratic equation in canonical form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.

core_formulas_rules.formula_or_law: Vieta's Formulas: Sum of roots = -b/a, Product of roots = c/a

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-11-math_ch_6_topic_6_1_introduction.detailed_overview: Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Preservation of distance, angle measures, and collinearity in plane geometric transformations.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.
• Sum of First n Terms (Series): S_n = (n/2)[2a_1 + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)[a_1 + a_n]. The sum equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of first and last terms.
key_points: The common difference d can be positive (increasing), negative (decreasing), or zero (constant sequence).
If the n-th term is linear in n (e.g. a_n = 3n + 5), the sequence is guaranteed to be arithmetic with d equal to the coefficient of n (d = 3).
The sum formula S_n is quadratic in n with no constant term: S_n = An² + Bn.

book-11-math_ch_6_topic_6_2_translations.topic_title: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_6_2_translations.unit_summary: Curriculum Study Notes: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules. • Curriculum Focus: T_v(x, y) = (x + a, y + b), composition of translations, and matrix representation.
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_6_2_translations.detailed_overview: 3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: T_v(x, y) = (x + a, y + b), composition of translations, and matrix representation.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
options: S = ∅ (No real solution)
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.topic_title: 6.4 Rotations About the Origin and General Centers
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Rotation matrices for angles 90, 180, 270, and general theta; center of rotation and clockwise vs counterclockwise.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.

book-11-math_ch_6_topic_introduction_to_.topic_title: Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_introduction_to_.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions (Unit 6: Unit 6: Transformations of the Plane). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_introduction_to_.detailed_overview:
Arithmetic progressions represent discrete linear growth. The sum formula discovered intuitively by Gauss pairs symmetrical terms equidistant from the ends, each pair summing to (a_1 + a_n).

Key Takeaway: The n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is linear (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d), and its sum is S_n = n/2(a_1 + a_n).

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Graduated tax brackets and tiered agricultural tariffs in Ethiopia use arithmetic stepped progressions.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.1 Introduction to Isometries and Rigid Motions
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Preservation of distance, angle measures, and collinearity in plane geometric transformations.
• Arithmetic Sequence Definition: A sequence where consecutive terms have a constant difference d: d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}. Recursive form: a_n = a_{n-1} + d.
• General n-th Term Formula: a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Any term can be expressed relative to a_m: a_n = a_m + (n - m)d.
• Arithmetic Means: Numbers inserted between two endpoints such that the entire sequence is arithmetic. The single arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/2.

book-11-math_ch_6_topic_translations__ve.topic_title: Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_translations__ve.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules (Unit 6: Unit 6: Transformations of the Plane). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_6_topic_translations__ve.detailed_overview:
3D vectors model spatial orientation, mechanical forces, and computer graphics geometry. The dot product measures collinear alignment, while the cross product computes rotational torques and plane normals.

Key Takeaway: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero (u·v = 0); cross product generates a vector orthogonal to both inputs.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight navigation paths at Bole International Airport and satellite orbital positioning for Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 rely on 3D vector coordinates.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
topics_covered.topic_title: 6.2 Translations: Vector Formulation and Coordinate Rules
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: T_v(x, y) = (x + a, y + b), composition of translations, and matrix representation.

• 3D Space Coordinates: Points defined by ordered triples (x, y, z). Distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2): d = √[(x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)² + (z_2 - z_1)²]. Midpoint M = ((x_1+x_2)/2, (y_1+y_2)/2, (z_1+z_2)/2).
• Vector Magnitude & Unit Vectors: Magnitude |v| = √(v_1² + v_2² + v_3²). Unit vector in direction of v: u = v / |v|. Standard basis vectors: i = (1,0,0), j = (0,1,0), k = (0,0,1).
• Scalar (Dot) Product: u · v = u_1·v_1 + u_2·v_2 + u_3·v_3 = |u||v| cos θ. Orthogonality Condition: u and v are perpendicular if and only if u · v = 0.
• Vector (Cross) Product: u × v is perpendicular to both u and v with direction given by right-hand rule. Magnitude: |u × v| = |u||v| sin θ (area of parallelogram). Computed via 3×3 determinant.
• Equations of Lines & Planes: Line through r_0 with direction vector v: r(t) = r_0 + t·v. Plane through (x_0, y_0, z_0) with normal vector n = (A, B, C): A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0.
key_points: Dot product produces a scalar number; cross product produces a perpendicular vector in 3D.
Cross product is anti-commutative: u × v = -(v × u). Parallel vectors have u × v = 0.
Two planes are parallel if their normal vectors are proportional, and perpendicular if n_1 · n_2 = 0.

topics_covered.title: 7.4 Measures of Dispersion: Variance and Standard Deviation
topics_covered.topic_title: 7.4 Measures of Dispersion: Variance and Standard Deviation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Range, mean absolute deviation, sample/population variance, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.
